items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: And Avery Parrish playing 'After Hours' and...

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. Well, I would be there for business, you know. I was there to listen, you know. Because I wasn't a dancer by any stretch of the imagination! I had trouble tapping my foot in time! But it was really nice.

There were so many, so many great things, you know. Then the jukeboxes were popular in the ice cream parlors. You know, you'd go by, take your girlfriend to buy some ice cream sodas and stuff, or milkshakes, and you'd play the jukebox. You know, I used to listen to the great records by Erskine Hawkins, "Tuxedo Junction," "Whispering Grass," and "Nona," and "Georgia Brown" with the Bascomb brothers playing tenor... There was two Bascomb brothers. Dud played the trumpet on "Tuxedo Junction"; I think he really wrote…
